commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Repetendium is a loud, flashy infinite roguelike where you play a duck or other characters with ridiculous guns, each starting with a fixed gun and ability. Runs continue as long as you survive while difficulty scales. He finds the first few hours very satisfying because you become overpowered fast, but says the content runs out after about four hours. A recent update added little. He calls it fun but repetitive and places it in high C tier.
praise: Very satisfying for the first few hours
Loud, flashy presentation with ridiculous guns
Many perks have unique mechanical designs, such as splitting bullets on a trigger
You feel overpowered very quickly if you find the right build
Levels come quickly, giving fast progression
criticism: Not enough content: after roughly four hours you have seen every boss, enemy, item and perk
Once the unique perks are collected, the rest are just stat number adjustments
Becoming powerful so fast makes it repetitive and he stopped paying attention to gameplay
Recent update added very little new content
Infinite structure needs more content to sustain it
unique_points: Infinite roguelike where a run lasts as long as you can survive, with scaling difficulty
Each character commits to one starting gun and ability for the entire run
commentary.quote: it's gonna be more like on a high C tier for me
design_criteria: Content volume: too little for an infinite structure
Perk design: unique mechanical perks praised, pure stat perks criticised
Power curve: becoming overpowered too fast causes disengagement
Repetition: same content seen after a few hours
Feel and presentation: loud, flashy, satisfying

community.one_liner: A top-down roguelite shooter from solo-ish indie studio Bearlex Games (Steam Early Access since Nov 2022) where you pick a character, dig through large cave stages, mine crystals and fight swarms and bosses while stacking weapons, mods and perks.
community.consensus_summary: Steam players rate it Very Positive (roughly 90-92% positive across about 220-300 reviews), but it is a tiny-audience title (Steam estimate of 20k-50k owners, only a handful of concurrent players) with no Metacritic or OpenCritic critic coverage at all. The sampled top-helpful English reviews skew heavily negative and are remarkably consistent: a great-feeling base (pixel art, music, humor, gameplay loop) that runs out of variety quickly, with the same maps, enemies and bosses repeating and very sharp difficulty spikes. The game is still in Early Access almost four years after launch. The developer kept shipping updates through mid-2025 and published a revised roadmap in Feb 2026, but has slipped the full-release target more than once. Critic-style validation is absent, so the verdict rests on players and on the developer's own update trail.
best_things: Strong pixel-art look, music and humor that land in the first runs (a reviewer who still gave a negative verdict praised all three)
Fast, satisfying core loop of shooting swarms, leveling up and stacking perks, in the survivors-like / twin-stick tradition
Low price (about $5.99) makes it feel like low risk; several reviewers say the price softens the disappointment and that it is worth trying for genre fans
Weapon modding and a perk/gem system give room for theorycrafting and min-maxing builds (one 15-hour reviewer says it is fun for chasing a specific build)
Several playable characters with distinct mechanics, e.g. a bear with a tank companion, Team Mischief as a group you drag around, and an auto-aim/auto-fire character for less precise players
Local co-op, full controller support, global leaderboards and a competitive scoring angle for players who like chasing ranks
Developer is visibly active and communicative: regular patch notes, new biomes (Enveloping Rime), new characters and a public roadmap
Random events add some variety inside runs (called fun even by a critical reviewer)
worst_things: Repetition: same large cave-style maps, same enemy set and same bosses recur across runs and even within a run, so runs feel alike after a few hours
Content is thin: reviewers cite about 3 characters and one repeated map at the time they wrote; several reviewers say it feels like a demo or tech demo at the current price
Upgrades feel flat: mostly plain stat boosts (damage, attack speed, accuracy) without real trade-offs or interesting interactions between weapons and skills

Steep difficulty spikes: enemy power jumps after the first level, elites are bullet sponges, and late-game enemies or modifiers (e.g. exploding enemies) can nearly one-shot even heavily defended builds
No real ending or goal to finish a run, so the game is scores and upgrades with no payoff; one reviewer contrasts it with Binding of Isaac for this reason
Stability complaints: reports of crashes during runs (including losing a long run while chasing an achievement), and one reviewer says it heavily taxes their PC
Levels look bland (walls, floors and crystal veins) and rooms can feel empty
Early Access has dragged on since Nov 2022; the full-release estimate of 2025 has passed (store page, not reviews)
improvements: More enemy and boss variety, including biome-specific enemy sets, so deeper floors do not just mean more of the same enemies
A real ending or win condition (and more biomes) so that runs and meta-progression have a finish line
Upgrade and build design with trade-offs and synergies rather than plain stat bumps; make weapon and ability choices feel meaningfully different
Rebalance difficulty (early ramp, ice biome, boss timer that fills too fast, elite damage) and make defense stats stay useful late
Fix crashes and add run recovery; make the no-upgrade score mode's rules and lack of unlocks clearer on the store page
Clearer communication on development pace and release timing (the Feb 2026 roadmap moves in this direction with a town hub, reworked upgrades, gear system and more biomes)
unique_things: Digging and crystal mining are built into level traversal; the crystal-wall mining is the one thing reviewers say sets it apart from other shooters (though some find it pointless or annoying)
Weapon modding plus a gem system on top of perks, rather than only passive pickups
Team Mischief character, a squad you lead and drag with a distance slider, and Orso with a tank companion and HQ assistance

Two distinct modes at launch: a roguelike mode with upgrades and unlocks and a score-focused mode with leaderboards, weekly/daily challenges (weekly mode slated for removal in the Feb 2026 roadmap) and a planned speedrun mode
Rover-style mining vehicle abilities and industrial weapons such as a sawblade launcher; Steam Inventory cosmetic drops
tedious_or_disliked: Meta-progression reads as grindy: one reviewer says grinding upgrades pushed the point of being overwhelmed back but added little new fun
Slow start and boring early perks; first few minutes of a run lack excitement
Being one-shot or killed by a single hit in an otherwise slow-paced run
Leaderboard-first-place achievements (later changed to top 5) were seen as unattainable and as a sign of priorities; suspected cheating on the boards was also mentioned
Digging through walls is called annoying by some players
Steam community threads complain about an ice biome that slows and punishes players and a boss timer that fills too fast
divisive_points: Auto-aim/auto-fire versus manual aiming: one reviewer found aiming too hard without auto-aim and auto-fire unsatisfying, others enjoy the survivors-like feel
Mining/digging: a signature feature to some, pointless busywork to others
Price vs content: praised as a cheap fun roguelite by some, called not worth it (compared unfavorably to Vampire Survivors at similar price) by others
Difficulty: some want a harder roguelike challenge, others find the spikes and one-shot deaths unfair
community.reception_notes: Launched into Steam Early Access on 4 Nov 2022 at a very low price with Windows only and no Mac/Linux. The store page says price will rise about 50% through Early Access. Launch-era reviews already flagged repetition, one-shot deaths, broken or badly designed leaderboard achievements, and a balance spike after the first level; the developer responded by changing the first-place achievements to top-5. Updates since: Team Mischief character (0.203, Jul 2024), second biome Enveloping Rime plus industrial weapon and mining vehicle (0.300 and 0.301, Nov 2024), Orso character (0.35, Dec 2024), Russian translation (0.36, Feb 2025), a progression tracker replacing the achievement screen and cosmetic Steam Inventory drops (0.361, Jun 2025), then a progress post in Aug 2025 and a quick roadmap update on 5 Feb 2026 (town hub menu, reworked upgrade system, gear system replacing weapon customization, weekly mode removed, speedrun mode added, characters cut from 8 to 6, up to 5 main biomes). The store page we fetched still said the last update was over 16 months ago and targeted a 2025 full release, so the full release is overdue. No Metacritic or OpenCritic reviews exist (the Metacritic page exists but is empty). Caveat: the Steam review sample we had access to had only two positive reviews (one-word or very short), so praise is inferred mostly from the aggregate score, the negative reviewers' own admissions, the store page and developer updates; there is no substantial independent press coverage found. Web search was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so Reddit and press coverage were not checked.
